A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Event Ellipsometer. Their complete main papers and supplements are readable, and the methods, equations, experiments, and visualizations can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic reconstruction experiments, measurements of known optical elements, and real demonstrations involving photoelasticity, human capture, transparent tape, and HDR scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds component ablations, reconstruction-stability measurements, external-method comparisons, and event-rate analyses.

M1.justification: The rotating-QWP system, event image-formation model, weighted SVD, Cloude filtering, propagation, perturbation, and calibration procedures remain unchanged. Component removals in the new ablations are evaluation variants.

E1.justification: The original synthetic and real scenes are retained. Supplement Section 4.4 adds a planar-scene simulation with ideal coaxial and realistic misaligned configurations for the single-shot comparison, extending the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds actual comparisons against Baek et al. (2020)'s frame-based approach and Zaidi et al. (2024)'s single-shot method in Supplement Sections 4.3–4.4. These methods were cited but not experimentally compared in v1, so this substantially expands external validation.

E3.justification: The new comparisons introduce exposure-bracketed HDR capture under 36 QWP-angle combinations and synthetic testing under ideal coaxial versus realistic misaligned configurations. These substantially expand the evaluation protocols; the original reconstruction budgets and synthetic-noise settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's synthetic pipeline-convergence analysis, v2 adds real-air ablations isolating Cloude filtering, propagation, and perturbation, plus temporal Mueller-matrix stability and single-shot alignment analyses. The original motor-speed plot is retained and relocated, rather than constituting an entirely new test.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports motor-speed standard deviations of 0.31 and 0.07 Hz and an across-scene event-rate standard deviation of 41.1 MEv/s. These add descriptive variability reporting. Both versions already report 15 threshold-calibration repetitions; no increase in repetitions is stated.

E6.justification: v2 adds real-sample MSEs of 0.016, 0.015, 0.013, 0.020, and 0.020 in main Figure 5, component-ablation values in Supplement Table 2, and baseline, stability, and event-rate results. Supplement Figure 8 reports MSEs of 0.408/0.133 for Zaidi's ideal/realistic configurations and 0.009 for Event Ellipsometer. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The image-formation, reconstruction, calibration, and Mueller-decomposition equations are retained. No substantive mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of normalized Mueller-matrix video acquisition at 30 fps, dynamic/HDR imaging, and the same system, calibration, and reconstruction contributions.

C2.justification: Supplement Section 5.3 newly explains the negligible-within-frame-motion assumption and failures when motion-induced events dominate, particularly in dark hair. v2 also interprets the component ablations and reconstruction stability under imperfect synchronization; the earlier wavelength and QWP-artifact limitations remain.

D1.justification: Captions for retained scenes newly disclose ROI dimensions and average event rates, including 600×600 for face/hair and 256×256 for tape. These improve capture documentation without establishing changed settings. The hardware list, reconstruction implementation, runtimes, and calibration instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained: Baek and Zaidi were already referenced in v1. New supplementary discussion develops the comparison with these approaches through acquisition time, metasurface cost, alignment sensitivity, and flexibility in light positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with localized wording corrections and added acknowledgments. The supplement organizes Additional Results into six subsections and adds a Motion Artifacts subsection, without extensive rewriting of retained material.

P2.justification: v2 adds Supplement Table 2 and Figures 6–8, relocates the motor-speed plot, and updates captions and main-figure annotations, including per-material MSEs. Existing scene visualizations are retained and renumbered; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The component ablations, frame-based comparison, stability measurements, and explicit motion limitations improve validation and transparency. However, the new comparisons cover a narrow set of scenes, and Supplement Figure 8's ideal/realistic baseline MSEs of 0.408/0.133 conflict with the accompanying misalignment-degradation narrative. This unresolved inconsistency limits the strength of the added comparative evidence.
